recipes.name: Margarita Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan.

To make the cake: Combine cake mix, pudding mix, eggs, oil, water, lemon juice, 1/4 cup tequila and 2 tablespoons triple sec in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes.

Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean, about 45 to 50 minutes. Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a cooling rack while you make the glaze.
To make the glaze: Combine confectioners' sugar, 1 tablespoon tequila, 2 tablespoons triple sec, and 2 tablespoons lime juice in a small bowl; mix until smooth. Pour glaze over cake while still warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Margarita Cake
raw_recipe.description: This margarita cake made with cake mix, tequila, lime juice, and triple sec is finished with a margarita-flavored glaze for a fabulous celebration cake!

video.description: When it’s time for a cake fiesta, serve up thick, flavorful slices of this delicious cocktail-flavored cake! You’ll love how easy it is to make, too! Combine an orange cake mix with an instant vanilla pudding mix, eggs, oil, water, lemon juice, tequila and triple sec. Bake for nearly an hour, then pour a glaze of confectioners’ sugar, tequila, triple sec and lime juice over the Bundt cake while it’s still warm. Then make a toast to the good life with every bite!

review.reviewBody: This cake turned out phenomenal! I changed the recipe quite a bit, so it would be more like a margarita. I used white cake mix, and used lime juice where it called for lemon juice. I made 2 separate batches of glaze. I also used top shelf liquor; Jose Cuervo and Grand Mariner instead of triple sec. Immediately when the cake came out of the oven I poked several holes in the cake and poured a shot of tequila over it, 2tbsp of grand mariner, and poured ½ of one of the batches of glaze on it as well. After allowing the cake to cool for 15 minutes I took the cake out of the pan and glazed the cake with the other half of the first batch of glaze. Finally, about an hour later I glazed it with the 2nd batch of glaze. I made this cake for a small, Mexican cuisine themed get together at my house, everyone loved it So easy, moist, flavorful and delicious! Will definitely make again!

Fabulous cake -- very moist. Like others, I couldn't find an orange cake mix, so used a lemon cake and substituted a combination of orange and lemon juice for the water and a tablespoon of orange oil. I agree that I'm not sure the tequila added much and will probably opt for using a margarita mix next time in place of it. I doubled the glaze, poked holes in the warm cake, and poured one recipe of glaze over the bottom while the cake was still in the pan; then added extra sifted powdered sugar to get the glaze to the consistency I wanted before drizzling it over the cake in three passes -- one while warm; one about 30 minutes later; and the last about an hour later. Very citrus-y and yummy. (The picture I added is after three days -- still moist and tasty!)

I only gave this cake four stars because I made some changes to the original recipe after reading some of the reviews. With the changes made I think it's a five star cake. Everyone loved it, even those that don't like margarita's. Will definitely make it again. 
I used yellow cake mix and topped it up to the required 18.25oz with orange cake mix. Using just a few ounces of orange cake mix gave it just a hint of orange flavour but a bit of an odd colour. Next time I'll use white cake mix and top up with orange. I substituted the oil with apple sauce and used lime juice instead of lemon juice. I also dusted my bundt pan with sieved orange cake mix.
The glaze is very good and after reading the reviews I made two batches of it. The first batch I made exactly as in the original recipe. I poured half of the batch over the cake when it was hot from the oven and still in the pan. The other half I poured over the cake when it had cooled down just enough for me to turn it out of the pan onto a rack. The second batch I made a little thicker by adding more sugar. Half of this I brushed on to the cake once it had completely cooled down. I thickened the remaining half even more (by adding more sugar) and added a drop or so of green food colouring. This half I drizzled on top of the cake. 
I made this for our 4th of July celebration and everybody loved it, but unfortunately I was so busy I forgot to take a picture of it!

I made this cake for a combo cinco de mayo-kentucky derby party. I was nervous bringing something that I had never made or tasted before but, based on all of the positive reviews, I decided to take a chance. Well, it was delicious. Like others, I made the following changes:
1. I didn't want to risk a flat cake so I bought 2 cake mixes to make sure I had the full 18.25 oz. (Cake mixes are now 15.25 oz) Bought a Duncan Hines Yellow cake mix and a cheap Walmart yellow cake mix to steal the extra 3 oz. I needed from.
2. Substituted yellow cake mix for orange.
3. Substituted margarita mix (non-alcoholic) for the water.
4. Substituted lime juice for lemon juice.
5. Substituted Grand Mariner for triple sec for both the cake and the glaze.

The cake baked up nice and full (filled the bundt pan - no flat cake!) Once out of the oven, I poked holes in it using the end of a wooden spoon and poured some glaze over it. About 10/15 min after that, I removed the cake from the pan onto a cooling rack. I placed a plate under the cooling rack to catch the glaze drippings...so I could put it back on the cake (don't want to waste a drop!) The glaze is thin so I made an extra batch and tried to thicken it by adding an extra cup of confectioners' sugar. It didn't come out as thick as I had hoped but it was an improvement (couldn't get it to look thick and white like the picture). Once the cake had cooled for an hour, I poured more glaze over the cake.

The cake was delicious.

If I could give this cake more starts I would. Rates right up there with the favorites now. I made it for a Bunko function. It was a huge hit. So moist and so good.



Notes: 
I actually made this twice, the first time I went to allrecipes.com and they had a couple suggestions.
One of them was when the cake 1st comes out of the oven, poke it with a fork all over and pour 1/2 of the icing into cake. After 10 min. Flip cake onto platter and use the other 1/2 (after poking fork holes and while cake is still warm).

I actually doubled the icing. (The first batch I split for the top/bottom while warm). The 2nd batch I modified so it was a bit thicker and poured over the top after the cake had cooler; prior to serving.

For the 2nd batch, I only used 1 T. of the Tequilla and Triple sec and the 2T of the lime juice. The icing is thinner than normal but it basically gets soaked into the cake. If you would like it thicker, add more powdered sugar.

I also grated lime all over the top. This cake was so moist. Enjoy!!!

This cake was a huge hit! I made some changes, however. Are used white cake mix, and I added one small box of lime Jell-O. I increase the water from 2/3 to 1 cup, and added an extra tablespoon of tequila to the cake mix. When I make this cake again, I will probably add an extra egg, as well. I made some changes, however. I used white cake mix, and I added one small box of lime Jell-O. I increase the water from 2/3 to one cup, and add an extra tablespoon of tequila to the cake mix. When I make this cake again, I will probably add an extra egg, as well. When the cake came out, I drizzle tequila on the bottom of it, since I used a Bundt cake pan. I would probably double the glaze and add the glaze to the pod bottom next time. As far as the glaze, I decrease the amount of lime juice, because it’s otherwise too thin. Alternatively, you could increase the amount of sugar but I’m not a fan of sugar. Once glazed, topped the cake with lime zest and rocksalt/margarita salt.

Made this for my daughter's birthday - she LOVES margaritas. I will say I had my reservations about it. Being an unconventional cake, I was worried the 10 or so people that were over wouldn't care for it. Seeing all the 5-star reviews gave me the push I needed to go ahead and make it and holy moly am I glad I did! I took into account a couple of changes I read about:
*I did use white cake as I couldn't find orange cake mix
*fresh lime juice in lieu of lemon juice
*I poked holes in the cake before unmolding it
*Doubled the glaze and poured some over the bottom to seep into the holes
*3 layers of glaze once unmolded and cooled on a rack
*after the third layer I sprinkled fresh lime zest over the top
I thought seriously about doing just a tiny sprinkle of salt as suggested but I chickened out. Next time I will try that and it will be soon as I had people already asking me to make this cake for one event or another.

Thank you, Carol, for a fabulous recipe!

Delicious with these changes: White cake mix, lemon pudding, lime instead of lemon juice, and double the glaze. For the moistest cake, poke holes in hot cake and pour 1/3 glaze over it while still in the pan, then wait 10 minutes, turn out cake, poke & glaze with another third (a pastry brush was helpful), then add more sugar to remaining glaze to thicken it and drizzle that over cooled cake.

I made this into cupcakes. One of the best I’ve ever had but with many alterations. I used white cake mix, lime juice instead of lemon juice, more tequila and triple sec and less water.I poked holes in the cupcakes when they came out of the oven and put the glaze on top of the cupcakes. Then I made a butter cream cream cheese lime frosting. One of the best cupcakes ever

Delicious! I didn’t have orange cake mix, so I just used yellow and substituted orange juice for the water. My glaze came out much thinner... so I just poured it on and then topped the cake with some 10X to make it look pretty.
 I’ve also made it with rum instead of tequila. This cake has been a big hit with my family and friends!
Delicious. I made double the icing, used fresh squeezed lime juice not lemon juice. Used two round cake pans, put icing between layers. Also brushed each layer with Triple Sec. Fabulous!

I baked the cake according to the instructions. It tastes great! I already had tequila and triple sec, so I didn't need to buy any. I served it as a dessert, with beef birria tacos as the main entree. I used Mexican rice and refried beans as side dishes.
Very good recipe for summer
Amazon has Duncan Hines orange cake mix. 👍🏻

I love this cake. Have made it for family gatherings, as well as work events. I love the original recipe, but I do substitute the tequila and triple sec with non-alcohol margarita mix. This keeps the flavors on spot, but makes the cake enjoyable for all.
Strawberry margarita cake

I made this cake with duck eggs, because I was given a couple and wanted to use them in a cake. It took me a while but I did find orange cake mix at a Woolworths (not all of them stock it). I couldn't find pudding mix anywhere though, so I used a panna cotta mix that I got at an Asian grocer. I used the icing mix that came with the orange cake and added coconut flavoured tequila blanco and Cointreau. I didn't have a bunt cake tin, so just used a square one I had. It turned out great! It did remind me of a margarita and it was dense by fluffy.
This is a delicious and easy cake to feed a crowd. I used lemon cake mix and lemon pudding. I also substituted lime juice for lemon juice
This cake is the freaking bomb! My friends and family couldn't get enough of it.

Where can you actually find orange cake mix? I used standard lemon like others. The resulting cake was delicious (great soft and moist consistency in particular) but was not reminiscent of margaritas at all. So it was tasty but not as festive as I hoped.
